overview: White plays the flank moves a4 and b4 against a King's Indian set-up, aiming for queenside space and a Polish-style queenside expansion. Black develops with ...Bg7 and ...d6 or ...c5, and fights back in the centre. The line is rare and read from the moves.

white_ideas.idea: Gain space with a4 and b4, then Bb2
Develop with e3 or g3 and keep a flexible centre

black_ideas.idea: Strike in the centre with ...c5 or ...d5
Build a fianchetto and a pawn centre

typical_structures.structure: White queenside pawns on a4 and b4 against Black's fianchetto set-up

character.notes: Flank expansion rather than forcing play, but it is not hard to break.

soundness.notes: Playable, with Black able to hit the advanced pawns.

level.notes: Few forcing lines to learn and plans are straightforward.
